subject: POC: prompt set & eval dataset collection — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC: prompt set & eval dataset collection — next steps

Emily — great to meet earlier. Thanks again for the time and for walking through Acme Health's use cases around clinical note summarization and triage assistance. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off the POC next week:

Summary of scope
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood inference for clinical note summarization at low latency while preserving PHI de-identification and accuracy on key metrics.
- Success criteria (proposed): >90% accuracy on clinician-labeled summary relevance, median generation latency < 450ms for 2k token context, and <=20% cost delta vs baseline per-API-unit.

POC deliverables / evaluation plan
- Acme provides: 500 de-identified prompt examples + 50 labeled gold summaries (for eval). Also a small sample of raw logs (10 full sessions) to validate KV cache behavior.
- Redwood provides: evaluation harness, suggested prompt set template, baseline runs on curated model variants, and a short report with metrics + recommended model/quantization.

Ownership & timeline
- Acme owner: Emily Zhao (data + prompts) and Paul Benson (security/infra).
- Redwood owner: Marissa Cole (product lead), Aditya Rao (ML infra/POC ops), Dev Patel (integration/ingest).
- Proposed timeline: week of Jul 6 — ingest & sample prep; week of Jul 13 — runs & iterative tuning; week of Jul 20 — final evaluation & recommendations.

Next steps for you (Emily)
1) Share the prompt set + gold summaries (CSV or XLSX) and one example raw log extract (10 sessions) with any PHI redaction notes.
2) Sign the attached POC template (low-key SOW) if the scope looks right.
3) Confirm the security contact (Paul) for the secure upload details.

I've attached a short POC template (redwood_poc_template.docx) that captures scope and timelines — feel free to redline. If it's easier, we can do a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the data format.

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Benson <paul.benson@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: prompt set & eval dataset collection — next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This looks good and aligns with our expectations. A couple of quick clarifications before we upload:

1) Prompt/gold format: We can export CSV with columns [prompt_id, prompt_text, gold_summary, note_redaction_flag]. Example attached (acme_prompt_samples.csv) — that has ~12 sample rows.
2) Logs: We can provide 10 session exports but security requires we de-identify at extract. Our infra team will remove PHI in advance and provide a short manifest describing the de-ident steps.
3) Timeline: Jul 6 ingestion start works for us. We may need a few days to prepare the de-id pipeline (Paul is looping in our security team).

I've attached the sample prompts. Paul — can you confirm who on your side will be the point for secure uploads? We prefer an S3 presigned method or secure upload link.

Also — curious on how you measure the "accuracy" metric. Can you share a short note on the eval harness and whether it supports multiple reference summaries?

Thanks,
Emily

Emily Zhao
Product Lead, Clinical AI | Acme Health
emily.zhao@acmehealth.com | (617) 555-0177

Attachment: acme_prompt_samples.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Paul Benson <paul.benson@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: prompt set & eval dataset collection — next steps

Thanks Emily — the sample looks great and the CSV layout is exactly what we need. Quick answers to your questions:

- Eval harness: We run a pairwise and n-gram overlap evaluation (ROUGE variants + BERTScore) and also compute a clinician relevance score when you provide a single gold summary per prompt. If you have multiple human references we can compute consensus metrics and use mean max scoring. We will include a calibration step so our thresholds align with your clinical team.
- Multiple references: supported — our harness accepts 1..N references per prompt (CSV with repeated prompt_id rows or a separate refs file).

On uploads: Aditya — can you share the secure upload instructions (S3 presigned or Redwood secure endpoint)? We'll need Paul to confirm acceptance.

Next steps from Redwood:
- We'll send a short ingestion spec (expected columns, encoding, how to attach multiple refs) and a secure upload link.
- We'll provision a small test workspace and run the 12 samples to ensure parsing is correct before you upload the full 500.

If Jul 6 start still looks good, let's lock a 30-min kickoff on Jul 6 (10:00am PT). I'll send a calendar invite.

—
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: prompt set & eval dataset collection — next steps

Hi Emily — quick technical notes on the ingest and de-id: 

1) File format: CSV or XLSX supported. For multiple references we prefer either a separate refs.csv or repeating prompt_id rows — we'll attach the ingest schema.
2) De-ID: good to hear you'll remove PHI upstream. Please include a short manifest.txt describing fields removed (e.g., names, MRNs) and sample redaction regexes if available.
3) Secure upload: we've provisioned a one-off secure upload link (short-lived presigned S3) for Acme. Please use the Redwood upload portal here: https://app.redwood.ai/upload/secure?token=abc123. If your S3 process needs presigned keys, we can generate them — let us know.
4) Sample logs: for the raw session logs, please compress (gz) and include sample timestamps. We'll only use them to validate cache/key behavior and will not persist any raw PHI.

I'll drop the ingest schema in the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcXyzPOC and will follow up with a minimal checklist for your infra team.

—
Aditya Rao
ML Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
